jsesh.mdcDisplayer.layout
Interface Layout

All Known Subinterfaces:
PagedLayout
All Known Implementing Classes:
AbstractLayout, SimplePrinterLayout
public interface Layout

Elements of this class are responsible for computing the position and dimensions of view elements.

A layout can change a view's width and height and it can also change the subview positions and scales.

Important - note that layout does just that -- layout -- and does in no way create view elements. MDCView element creation is the task of ViewBuilder.

An actual base for implementation can be found in the SimpleLayout class.

Author:
Serge Rosmorduc

layout

public void layout(MDCView view,
                   int depth)
compute the view size (width and height). If the view has subviews, layout should compute their position in the parent view and scale them if required. Note that layout is not a recursive function : when a view is built, its subviews have already been processed by another call to layout. The embedded variable is used to specify that this view corresponds to an element that doesn't appears on the upper levels of the text. For instance, it will be true for a cadrat, but false when this cadrat is embedded within another cadrat. In fact that's the main use of this variable, as spacing can be quite different (specially in columns).

Parameters:
view -
depth - the depth of the view.

preLayoutHook

public void preLayoutHook(MDCView view,
                          int depth)
This method is called before anything is done on the view. Most notably, it's called before the subviews are built. It might be used when the layout of the internal elements depends on their container.

It can also be used for things which should be done to all views.

Currently, its main actual use is to change the sign centering preferences when laying out a cadrat.

Parameters:
view -
depth - depth of the view. the view for the whole text has depth 0.

postLayoutHook
